## (50 points) 1. USDA Data Visualization Portfolio
Use the USDA datasets (worked on in class) to come up with a new visualization of the data with the variables provided, making sure you use joins. The visualization should incorporate different variables than what we worked on in class. Create a data-rich visualization as possible, according to the following steps in the quarto file.


**Your group may all work together and submit the same visualization, but each person needs to submit by pushing to their repo.**


```{r}
# Location of the excel file:
url <- 'https://ers.usda.gov/sites/default/files/_laserfiche/DataFiles/48747/Unemployment.xlsx?v=58453'

# Name of the file to save:
destfile <- "Unemployment.xlsx"

# Download
curl::curl_download(url, destfile)
unemployment <- readxl::read_excel(destfile,
                                        skip = 4,
                                        sheet = 'UnemploymentMedianIncome')

glimpse(unemployment)

```

```{r}
# Location of the excel file:
url <- 'https://ers.usda.gov/sites/default/files/_laserfiche/DataFiles/48747/Education.xlsx?v=14208'

# Name of the file to save:
destfile <- "Education.xlsx"

# Download
curl::curl_download(url, destfile)
education <- readxl::read_excel(destfile,
                                        skip = 3,
                                        sheet = 'Education 1970 to 2022')

glimpse(education)

```

Now working with your group:

(1) Find a way to join the `unemployment` and `education` datasets together.
(2) Create an informative data visualization.
